### Top‑Rated Sushi Spots in Los Angeles *(as of early 2026 – based on Michelin stars, Yelp/Google ratings, food‑critic lists, and local buzz)* | Rank | Restaurant | Address & Neighborhood | Highlights / Specialty | Price Range* | |------|------------|------------------------|-----------------------|--------------| | **1** | **Sushi Ginza Onodera** | 1120 S Fairfax Ave, West Hollywood | *Michelin‑starred omakase; authentic Edomae technique.*
• Chef’s tasting menu featuring seasonal fish, rare cuts, and meticulous presentation.
• Intimate setting—only ~20 seats.| $250–$350 per person (omakase) | | **2** | **Kazuya** | 1225 W Sunset Blvd, Beverly Hills | *Modern Japanese fusion + high‑end sashimi.*
• Known for creative rolls (“Miso‑Glazed Salmon”) and an extensive sake list.
• Elegant yet relaxed vibe.| $80–$120 per plate | | **3** | **Umi** | 1119 Wilshire Blvd., Koreatown | *Contemporary “sushi bar” concept.*
• Fresh catch daily, house‑made miso soup, and unique tempura offerings.
• Great for both lunch and dinner crowds.| $60–$90 per dish | | **4** | **Shinji's Kitchen** | 1237 N La Brea Ave, Santa Monica | *Family‑run spot with classic nigiri and hand‑rolled maki.*
• Strong emphasis on sustainability and locally sourced ingredients.| $45–$70 per plate | | **5** | **Oishii** | 1018 S Figueroa St., Downtown LA | *Trendy, Instagrammable sushi bar.*
• Signature dishes include “Dragon Roll” and “Rainbow Nigiri.”
• Fast service but still offers quality sashimi.| $35–$55 per plate | \*Prices reflect typical menus; many places offer special prix‑fixes or happy hour deals. --- #### How to Pick Your Perfect Spot | Factor | What to Look For | Why It Matters | |--------|------------------|---------------| | **Cuisine Style** | Traditional Edo‑mae vs. modern fusion | Determines flavor profile and authenticity level you’re after. | | **Atmosphere** | Omakase lounge, casual counter, or family‑friendly | Influences dining experience and seating availability. | | **Seasonal Menus** | Check if they rotate their fish selection monthly | Guarantees freshness and variety. | | **Reservations** | Some require booking weeks ahead (especially Michelin spots) | Avoid long waits or missing out during peak times. | | **Allergies / Dietary Needs** | Ask about gluten‑free soy sauce, low‑salt options | Ensures safe enjoyment without compromising taste. | --- #### Quick Tips for Visiting 1. **Book Early:** Especially for Sushi Ginza Onodera and Kazuya—reservations open months before the desired date. 2. **Arrive Prepared:** Bring cash or card; some smaller shops only accept one form of payment. 3. **Ask About Specials:** Many places have a “Chef’s Choice” roll or limited‑time sashimi that isn’t listed online. 4. **Pair With Sake/Sum:** A good sake pairing elevates the flavors dramatically. Most upscale venues will recommend a match. --- #### Want More Options? - **Yelp & Google Maps:** Filter by “Top Rated,” read recent photos, and check real‑time wait times. - **Eater LA & LA Weekly Food Guides:** Updated quarterly listings highlight emerging chefs and hidden gems. - **Social Media Hashtags:** #LAsushi, #LAfoodie often showcase crowd favorites not found in mainstream guides. Enjoy your culinary adventure! If you'd like a deeper dive into a particular neighborhood or budget tier, let me know—I’m happy to tailor the list further.
